title: CRLN per-language clinical research term list
description: One file per language, crln-terms-<lang>.json. The source of truth for every machine translation into that language. ops/scripts/gen-terminology-module.py derives each app's _shared/terminology.ts from these files; nothing downstream is hand-edited.

language.description: The language code the translators receive, e.g. fi, pt-BR.

reviewer.description: Named reviewer for the language, or null before one agrees.

review_basis.description: What the reviewer actually reviewed, so a reader can check the reviewer rows against it.

id.description: Stable. Never renumber; a reviewer's decision column refers to it.

en.description: The English concept, as the reviewer should read it.

triggers.description: English forms that mean this concept is present. Lowercase: case-insensitive at the start of a word. ALL CAPS: whole-word acronym, case-sensitive. re:<regex>: a regular expression.

source_en.description: One real English sentence where the term occurs.

source_en_origin.description: reviewer: the line from the reviewer's sheet. content: picked from the published content by terminology-frequency.py.

target.description: The required rendering. For keep_english rows, the English form that must be kept.

status.description: confirmed and keep_en are reviewer rulings and are binding. proposed is ours and never enforced.

context.description: all, site-facing or participant-facing. Some concepts need different words on the two surfaces.

display.description: The forbidden rendering as a reader would write it.

stem.description: Matched anywhere in a word of the translation, so inflections and compounds are both caught. Keep stems long enough to be unambiguous.

pattern.description: A regular expression instead of a stem, for forms a stem cannot express.

enforce.description: True: a translation containing it fails the post-check, on reviewer rows only.

unless_source.description: Triggers that switch the rule off when present in the English, e.g. patient for potilas.
